prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
Do not attribute the syndrome to alcohol alone: the lobar frontal and anterior temporal atrophy and the behavioural profile are not explained by alcohol-related brain damage.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state which features are present, the functional decline, and the level of certainty (possible or probable).

Explain why alcohol-related brain damage does not account for the progressive syndrome, and manage the escalating alcohol use as part of the behavioural change (limit access, involve his wife, support abstinence).
Address safety and capacity: driving, finances (over $14,000 in impulsive online purchases: restrict access to cards and accounts) and lasting power of attorney while he can still take part.
Arrange caregiver education and support, and a plan for behavioural symptoms that avoids cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine.
Offer genetic counselling before any genetic test, and discuss what a result would mean for relatives.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not part of the FTD work-up; FDG-PET, or perfusion SPECT where it is unavailable, is the functional study used when needed.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; mild symmetric rigidity without bradykinesia or tremor does not call for it, and it would not change the diagnosis.

accepted: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic

differential.key_features: Bedside recall and clock are impaired, but memory is of retrieval type with normal recognition, the hippocampi are normal and the atrophy is frontal and anterior temporal with posterior sparing; an amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.

differential.diagnosis: Primary psychiatric disorder (late-onset mood or personality disorder)
differential.key_features: No psychiatric history; new behaviour at 56 with functional decline, frontal release signs, utilisation behaviour and lobar atrophy is not explained by a primary psychiatric disorder.

Recent escalation to 6-8 beers nightly, but no ataxia, ophthalmoplegia or neuropathy; loss of empathy, compulsions and knife-blade lobar atrophy are not the pattern of alcohol-related damage, and the drinking is itself part of the change in oral behaviour.

differential.diagnosis: Atypical parkinsonian syndrome with frontal behaviour (PSP, corticobasal syndrome)
differential.key_features: Mild symmetric rigidity, hypomimia and reduced arm swing, but no bradykinesia, gaze palsy, falls, limb apraxia or asymmetry.
Shuffling gait, but no urinary incontinence; ventricular enlargement is proportionate to the frontal atrophy.
Normal bulk and full strength, and no bulbar symptoms are described; nothing on examination suggests motor neuron disease.

key_clinical_evidence: Five of the six Rascovsky features on his wife's account (disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, compulsive behaviour, hyperorality), with loss of work and of self-care, meet possible bvFTD with significant functional decline.
Severe bilateral frontal and anterior temporal atrophy with a knife-blade pattern, normal hippocampi and preserved posterior cortex on MRI give the imaging support for probable bvFTD.
Neuropsychology shows severe executive and social-cognition deficits with a retrieval-type memory deficit, normal recognition and preserved visuospatial perception.
The frontal and anterior temporal pattern with relative posterior sparing makes Alzheimer disease less likely; an amyloid or CSF AD biomarker study is optional if doubt remains.
Mild symmetric rigidity without rest tremor or bradykinesia is compatible with bvFTD and does not by itself call for dopamine transporter imaging.
The escalation of alcohol intake belongs to the change in oral behaviour; it does not explain the lobar atrophy, the compulsions or the loss of empathy.

results.finding: Three of six core features within the first three years define possible bvFTD.
Probable bvFTD requires functional decline and supportive imaging.
Primary psychiatric disorders are the commonest misdiagnosis.

Behavioural variant FTD diagnosis and ma.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. Psychiatric disorders are the main mimics and are excluded on course and examination rather than on a single test. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

patient.history_present_illness:
Mr. K. is a 58-year-old right-handed White male brought in by his wife of 30 years for progressive personality and behavioral changes over the past 2 years. His wife reports that the change began subtly — he became less interested in conversation, more irritable, and started making inappropriate comments at family gatherings. Over the following year, the changes became unmistakable: he began making sexually explicit remarks to female neighbors, laughed at his granddaughter's injury, and showed complete indifference when their dog died. She describes him as having 'lost his soul.' He has developed compulsive behaviors: he insists on eating the same three meals daily, paces the living room for exactly 30 minutes every evening, and has begun hoarding items from grocery stores. His diet has changed dramatically — he craves sweets and high-calorie foods and has gained 18 pounds. His personal hygiene is severely degraded; his wife must physically guide him to shower.

Professionally, he retired from accounting 2 years ago after colleagues reported he was making errors in client accounts and had made inappropriate comments to staff. He shows no insight into his deficits and is not distressed. His wife has discovered he has been making online purchases totaling over $14,000, mostly buying things that he immediately forgets having ordered. His alcohol use has escalated from 1-2 beers a night to 6-8 beers nightly, which he denies entirely. He has never had psychiatric illness and there is no family history of dementia. Neurological review of systems is otherwise negative.

neurological_exam.additional: Hyperorality observed during exam — patient took crackers from desk without being offered. Poor hygiene noted by examiner: food stains on clothing, body odor.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Mild bilateral facial hypomimia noted.
neurological_exam.gait: Mildly shuffling, reduced arm swing. No apraxia.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but severely disinhibited throughout the exam. Makes inappropriate sexual comments to the female medical assistant. Laughs inappropriately when discussing his job loss. MMSE 21/30 — loses 3 points on delayed recall (0/3), 3 points on serial sevens, 2 points on orientation to date and month. Cannot copy interlocking pentagons (perseverates on strokes). Clock drawing severely abnormal: numbers placed randomly outside clock face. FAB 10/18 — fails go/no-go, environmental autonomy, conflicting instructions, and lexical fluency. Category fluency (animals): 7 in 60 seconds (severely impaired). Cannot explain proverbs (concrete interpretation). Utilization behavior: automatically picks up pen on desk and begins writing without instruction.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk. Mild bilateral upper extremity rigidity (cogwheel quality) without tremor. No bradykinesia on repetitive finger tapping. Strength 5/5 throughout.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ bilaterally. Bilateral grasp reflex present. Snout and palmomental reflexes present bilaterally (frontal release signs).
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally.
